Text.name: guidelines
Text.value: Read the question and answer, then determine if it contains the following features:

Text.name: humor_step1_header
Text.value: 🎯 STEP 1: Look for JOKES.

Text.name: humor_step1_q
Text.value: Does the text contain any of these?

Text.name: humor_step1_item1
Text.value: - A joke with a punchline

Text.name: humor_step1_item2
Text.value: - A pun or wordplay

Text.name: humor_step1_item3
Text.value: - A reference to movies, TV, or pop culture used to be funny

Text.name: humor_step1_item4
Text.value: - A sarcastic or mocking comment

Text.name: humor_step1_ex_header
Text.value: ✓ EXAMPLES of jokes (Mark Yes):

Text.name: humor_step1_ex1
Text.value: - 'Schrodinger's cat walks into a bar... and doesn't' (joke about superposition in quantum physics)

Text.name: humor_step1_ex2
Text.value: - 'Pluto was demoted to dwarf planet - talk about a mid-life crisis' (personification joke)

Text.name: humor_step1_ex3
Text.value: - 'If you think nobody cares about you, try missing a few tax payments' (sarcastic observation)

Text.name: humor_step1_result
Text.value: If you found a joke → Mark Yes. Otherwise continue to Step 2.

Text.name: humor_step2_header
Text.value: 😏 STEP 2: Look for IRONY or SARCASM.

Text.name: humor_step2_q
Text.value: Does the text contain any of these?

Text.name: humor_step2_item1
Text.value: - Saying the opposite of what you mean to be funny

Text.name: humor_step2_item2
Text.value: - Making something serious sound unimportant on purpose (understatement)

Text.name: humor_step2_item3
Text.value: - A side comment in brackets or parentheses that is dismissive or mocking

Text.name: humor_step2_item4
Text.value: - Colorful or silly imagery used in a serious context (the contrast is funny)

Text.name: humor_step2_item5
Text.value: - Dark humor: violent, morbid, or extreme language used casually for shock value

Text.name: humor_step2_ex_header
Text.value: ✓ EXAMPLES of irony (Mark Yes):

Text.name: humor_step2_ex1
Text.value: - 'The surgery went well, apart from the patient dying' (dark understatement)

Text.name: humor_step2_ex2
Text.value: - 'It's perfectly safe, unless you count the possibility of horrible death' (dark humor - casual mention of death)

Text.name: humor_step2_ex3
Text.value: - 'Nature is beautiful, if you ignore all the things trying to eat you' (dark humor - unexpected violent twist)

Text.name: humor_step2_ex4
Text.value: - 'String theory (which nobody actually understands)' (dismissive side comment)

Text.name: humor_step2_ex5
Text.value: - 'You'd basically become a very expensive puddle' about extreme pressure (silly image + serious topic)

Text.name: humor_step2_result
Text.value: If you found irony or sarcasm → Mark Yes. Otherwise continue to Step 3.

Text.name: humor_step3_header
Text.value: 🤪 STEP 3: Look for RIDICULOUS comparisons.

Text.name: humor_step3_desc1
Text.value: Does the text make a comparison that is SO silly or extreme that it's meant to be funny?

Text.name: humor_step3_desc2
Text.value: The humor comes from the absurdity - the comparison is intentionally too extreme or too silly.

Text.name: humor_step3_ex_header
Text.value: ✓ EXAMPLES of ridiculous comparisons (Mark Yes):

Text.name: humor_step3_ex1
Text.value: - 'Saying magnets work by magic is like saying cars run on wishes' (exaggerated comparison)

Text.name: humor_step3_ex2
Text.value: - 'Expecting your immune system to fight off everything is like expecting one security guard to defend a shopping mall from an army' (absurd scale mismatch)

Text.name: humor_step3_ex3
Text.value: - 'The odds are about the same as finding a specific grain of sand on every beach on Earth' (comically extreme)

Text.name: humor_step3_result
Text.value: If you found a ridiculous comparison meant to amuse → Mark Yes. Otherwise continue to Step 4.

Text.name: humor_step4_header
Text.value: ✗ STEP 4: Check it's NOT just vivid language.

Text.name: humor_step4_desc
Text.value: The following are NOT humor - they are just good explanations:

Text.name: humor_step4_not1
Text.value: - Normal comparisons: 'DNA is like a blueprint', 'electricity flows like water'

Text.name: humor_step4_not2
Text.value: - Lively descriptions: 'neurons firing like a symphony'

Text.name: humor_step4_not3
Text.value: - Personification: 'the virus hijacks the cell'

Text.name: humor_step4_not4
Text.value: - Enthusiastic tone without actual jokes

Text.name: humor_final_header
Text.value: ⚖️ FINAL DECISION:

Text.name: humor_final1
Text.value: - If you found a joke, irony, sarcasm, or ridiculous comparison in Steps 1-3 → Mark Yes

Text.name: humor_final2
Text.value: - If you only found vivid language or good explanations → Mark No

Text.name: conn_step1_header
Text.value: 🎨 1. Check if the answer contains a NAMED reference from popular culture.

Text.name: conn_step1_desc
Text.value: Mark Yes - Any of the following:

Text.name: conn_step1_item1
Text.value: - Named TV shows, movies, books, documentaries (e.g., 'Friends', 'Game of Thrones', 'The Matrix')

Text.name: conn_step1_item2
Text.value: - Named magazines, newspapers, publications (e.g., 'Time Magazine', 'Vogue', 'BBC')

Text.name: conn_step1_item3
Text.value: - Named historical figures commonly known (e.g., 'Napoleon', 'Julius Caesar', 'Cleopatra')

Text.name: conn_step1_item4
Text.value: - Named historical events (e.g., 'the French Revolution', 'the Renaissance')

Text.name: conn_step1_item5
Text.value: - Named brands, products, companies (e.g., 'Google', 'Netflix', 'Amazon')

Text.name: conn_step1_item6
Text.value: - Named games (e.g., 'Monopoly', 'Scrabble', 'basketball')

Text.name: conn_step1_item7
Text.value: - Pop culture jokes or memes (e.g., references to viral internet moments)

Text.name: conn_step1_item8
Text.value: - Famous landmarks (e.g., 'crowded like Times Square', 'tall as the Eiffel Tower')

Text.name: conn_step2_header
Text.value: 🍳 2. ALSO Mark Yes: Concrete everyday activities that people commonly do.

Text.name: conn_step2_desc1
Text.value: These are relatable human experiences that ground abstract concepts in daily life.

Text.name: conn_step2_desc2
Text.value: The activity must be something a general audience does or understands from personal experience.

Text.name: conn_step2_ex_header
Text.value: ✓ Mark Yes EXAMPLES:

Text.name: conn_step2_ex1
Text.value: - Household tasks: 'like doing laundry', 'similar to washing dishes', 'like vacuuming'

Text.name: conn_step2_ex2
Text.value: - Errands: 'like mailing a letter', 'similar to shopping for groceries', 'like waiting at the DMV'

Text.name: conn_step2_ex3
Text.value: - Food & cooking: 'like mixing ingredients for a cake', 'similar to marinating meat', 'like seasoning a soup'

Text.name: conn_step2_ex4
Text.value: - Social activities: 'like hosting a dinner party', 'similar to playing board games with friends'

Text.name: conn_step2_ex5
Text.value: - Common experiences: 'like getting stuck in traffic', 'similar to waiting for your coffee to brew'

Text.name: conn_step2_ex6
Text.value: - Work/school: 'like organizing your desk', 'similar to studying for an exam'

Text.name: conn_step2_key
Text.value: KEY: The activity must be EXTERNAL to the scientific topic being explained.

Text.name: conn_step2_key2
Text.value: It should make the reader think 'Oh, I know what that's like!'

Text.name: conn_step3_header
Text.value: ✗ 3. Mark No - The following do NOT count:

Text.name: conn_step3_abstract_header
Text.value: ABSTRACT ANALOGIES (too generic):

Text.name: conn_step3_abstract1
Text.value: - Natural phenomena: 'like a river flowing', 'like waves in the ocean', 'like a pebble dropping'

Text.name: conn_step3_abstract2
Text.value: - Abstract physics: 'like a ball rolling downhill', 'like a spring bouncing'

Text.name: conn_step3_abstract3
Text.value: - Generic objects: 'like a sponge absorbing', 'like a balloon inflating'

Text.name: conn_step3_also_header
Text.value: ALSO Mark No:

Text.name: conn_step3_also1
Text.value: - Scientific terminology (e.g., 'mitochondria', 'quantum entanglement', 'oxidation')

Text.name: conn_step3_also2
Text.value: - Technical concepts without cultural grounding (e.g., 'the process involves hydrolysis')

Text.name: conn_step3_also3
Text.value: - Vague references (e.g., 'as we all know', 'in everyday life', 'people often')

Text.name: conn_step3_also4
Text.value: - References already embedded in the original question

Text.name: conn_step3_also5
Text.value: - Geographic/astronomical names used technically (e.g., 'the Pacific plate', 'the Andromeda galaxy')

Text.name: conn_step3_also6
Text.value: - Answers with no cultural or everyday life references at all

Text.name: conn_step4_header
Text.value: ⚠️ 4. IMPORTANT: Everyday content directly relevant to the question topic does NOT count as a connection.

Text.name: conn_step4_desc1
Text.value: A 'connection to everyday life' must bring in something EXTERNAL to the topic being discussed.

Text.name: conn_step4_desc2
Text.value: If the everyday reference is just part of answering the question, it's not a connection.

Text.name: conn_step4_score0_header
Text.value: ✗ Mark No EXAMPLES (content is directly relevant to question):

Text.name: conn_step4_score0_ex1
Text.value: - Question about babies → mentioning 'breastfeeding' or 'diapers' (directly relevant, not a connection)

Text.name: conn_step4_score0_ex2
Text.value: - Question about cooking → mentioning 'your kitchen stove' (directly relevant, not a connection)

Text.name: conn_step4_score0_ex3
Text.value: - Question about cars → mentioning 'your gas tank' (directly relevant, not a connection)

Text.name: conn_step4_score0_ex4
Text.value: - Question about sleep → mentioning 'your bed' or 'pajamas' (directly relevant, not a connection)

Text.name: conn_step4_score10_header
Text.value: ✓ Mark Yes EXAMPLES (content brings in external reference):

Text.name: conn_step4_score10_ex1
Text.value: - Question about physics → mentioning 'like a scene from Interstellar' (external movie reference)

Text.name: conn_step4_score10_ex2
Text.value: - Question about biology → mentioning 'like that episode of House M.D.' (external TV reference)

Text.name: conn_step4_score10_ex3
Text.value: - Question about chemistry → mentioning 'like mixing ingredients for a cake' (external everyday activity)

Text.name: conn_step5_header
Text.value: ⚖️ 5. Mark Yes if ANY item from steps 1-2 is present AND it passes the test in step 4.

Text.name: conn_step5_desc
Text.value: Mark No otherwise.

Text.name: conn_step5_final_header
Text.value: FINAL EXAMPLES:

Text.name: conn_step5_final1
Text.value: - 'like a factory assembly line' → Mark No (generic analogy)

Text.name: conn_step5_final2
Text.value: - 'like a scene from Jurassic Park' → Mark Yes (named movie, external to topic)

Text.name: conn_step5_final3
Text.value: - 'like mailing a package' → Mark Yes (concrete everyday activity, external to topic)

Text.name: conn_step5_final4
Text.value: - 'like water flowing downhill' → Mark No (abstract nature analogy)
